open_points.subject: MCP action surface
open_points.text: “The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.” This omits the separately named primary actions to add or capture trial cases, release failed runs, roll back slots, propose bindings, and compose/prove flows, and calls `activate` an owner's operation although “agent or owner asks” for read-only activation.
open_points.question: Which distinct MCP operations exist, which primary actions are folded into `author` or another operation, and may an agent request activation of a proven read-only flow?
options: Every primary action is a distinct MCP operation, including agent-requested read-only activation
The omitted actions are sub-operations of `author` or `inspect`, with their stated actor permissions
K-11's shorter list is authoritative, so omitted actions or agent activation do not exist
open_points.default_guess: Expose every primary action explicitly and allow agents to request activation only for proven read-only versions.

open_points.subject: ContractVersion.issued_by
open_points.text: The candidate field is `issued_by`, while the source says “Issued by the kernel on an agent's request” and K-15 requires each agent's actions and the kernel's own actions to be distinguishable in every record.
open_points.question: Does `issued_by` name the requesting agent or the kernel that minted the version, and where is the other actor recorded?
options: `issued_by` is the kernel and a separate requester fact records the agent
`issued_by` is the kernel and the requesting agent is not recorded
open_points.default_guess: Record the requesting agent as `issued_by`, treating minting as mechanical behavior rather than a separate action.

open_points.subject: TrialExecution
open_points.text: M07 records `trial_execution_id`, `implementation_id`, `trial_case_id`, outcome, outputs, resources and `executed_at`, but no actor, although trials may be requested by an agent or run by the kernel during admission and K-15 says “The owner's actions, each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record.”
open_points.question: What fact distinguishes an agent-requested trial execution from a kernel-run admission execution, including which agent requested the former?
options: Add an initiating actor and an execution purpose or admission reference
Infer kernel execution from AdmissionVerdict membership and add an actor only for standalone trials
Do not record the initiating actor despite K-15
open_points.default_guess: Record the initiating actor and whether the execution belongs to an admission or a standalone trial.

open_points.subject: ProofResult
open_points.text: M17 says “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result,” but M14 says proof refuses a binding that is not `accepted`, and the carried State 2 decision says a version that failed for an unaccepted binding can be proven again later and succeed.
open_points.question: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can have different results as referenced binding statuses change?
options: Treat each proof as an observation with its own identity and decision-time dependency snapshot
Treat ProofResult as a value identified by the complete result plus the binding-state facts used
Keep only the latest computed result and give ProofResult no persistent identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a non-persisted value determined by the flow version plus the referenced binding states used for that proof.

open_points.subject: capture failed execution
open_points.text: Capture refuses an execution “whose run was already released (its files are gone),” and M06 repeats only that exclusion, while K-10 says every non-`failed` run's spool is emptied when the run ends, including `refused` and `cancelled` runs.
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ends `refused` or `cancelled`, particularly when its inputs included files whose bytes have already been removed?
options: Capture is allowed only while every referenced input payload still exists
Capture is allowed after any unreleased run, requiring non-failed runs to retain needed files
Capture is allowed after `refused` or `cancelled` only for executions whose inputs contain no files
Only executions belonging to a final `failed` run may be captured
open_points.default_guess: Allow capture only when all required input payloads still exist; after `refused` or `cancelled`, that permits value-only cases but not cases needing removed files.

open_points.subject: Installation
open_points.text: M28 declares Installation's identity to be `value` and its lifecycle `None`, but also says “the token list is read again whenever it has changed,” so configuration facts can change while the kernel continues running.
open_points.question: Does a token-list change replace the Installation with a new configuration value, or mutate one continuing installation entity, and is that change represented anywhere in kernel records?
options: Installation is a stable entity with mutable current configuration
Each reload creates a new Installation value or revision that subsequent actions use
Installation is an unrecorded live configuration view whose value identity has no operational use
open_points.default_guess: Treat the installation as a stable deployment identity with versioned configuration snapshots, while actor records continue to identify agents by name.
